sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Oh God!
sentences.zh: 天哪！

sentences.en: Thank you!
sentences.zh: 谢谢！

sentences.en: Thank you!
sentences.zh: 谢谢！

sentences.en: Thank you!
sentences.zh: 谢谢！

sentences.en: My whole damn life has been worth it just for this moment.
sentences.zh: 为了这一刻，我这辈子受的苦都值了。

sentences.en: So I was once walking the city with my friend Kathleen, who is an environmental scientist,
sentences.zh: 有一次我和朋友凯瑟琳在城里散步，她是一位环境科学家，

sentences.en: and she was pointing out the spray-painted markings of letters and arrows that you see everywhere on the street.
sentences.zh: 她指着街上随处可见的喷漆字母和箭头标记给我看。

sentences.en: The markings indicate where utility lines are running underground so they're not damaged by construction.
sentences.zh: 这些标记标示了地下公用设施管线的走向，以免施工时造成损坏。

sentences.en: And it turns out they're color-coded by the American Public Works Association.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，它们是按照美国公共工程协会的颜色代码来喷涂的。

sentences.en: Red spray-paint means electrical power lines and yellow is natural gas.
sentences.zh: 红色喷漆代表电力线，黄色代表天然气管道。

sentences.en: And I'm looking this up now on Wikipedia because I don't remember all the details.
sentences.zh: 我现在正在维基百科上查，因为我记不清所有细节了。

sentences.en: Green means sewage and drainage lines.
sentences.zh: 绿色代表污水和排水管道。

sentences.en: So public works people and construction crews have their own lo-fi augmented reality scribbled right on the street,
sentences.zh: 所以公共工程人员和施工队在街上直接涂写了属于他们自己的低保真增强现实，

sentences.en: like a giant map in plain sight.
sentences.zh: 就像一张显而易见的巨型地图。

sentences.en: It's a different way to see the city.
sentences.zh: 这是看待城市的一种不同方式。

sentences.en: But it's not just utility workers.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅是公用设施工人的事。

sentences.en: The city also reads differently depending on your knowledge, your experience,
sentences.zh: 城市也会根据你的知识、经验，

sentences.en: or if you happen to be standing on a rolling plank of wood.
sentences.zh: 或者你是否恰好站在一块滑动的木板上，而呈现出不同的面貌。

sentences.en: I've been lucky enough to go to these amazing places like Taiwan or L.A.,
sentences.zh: 我有幸去过台湾或洛杉矶这些神奇的地方，

sentences.en: but I only ever get to see, like, the weird places that skaters go to,
sentences.zh: 但我看到的永远只是滑板手会去的那些奇怪的地方，

sentences.en: like industrial parks or some handrail in the middle of a school somewhere.
sentences.zh: 比如工业园区，或者学校中间的某个扶手。

sentences.en: That's our guide today, skateboard photographer and radio reporter, Andrew Norton.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们今天的向导，滑板摄影师兼电台记者，安德鲁·诺顿。

sentences.en: My friend Ariel and I are skating in downtown Toronto, kind of carving through the big, empty corporate plazas.
sentences.zh: 我和朋友阿里尔正在多伦多市中心滑板，穿梭在那些巨大、空旷的企业广场中。

sentences.en: It's hard with a backpack.
sentences.zh: 背着背包很难滑。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'll give you one of these, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我可以给你一个这个。

sentences.en: To a skateboarder, the city looks different.
sentences.zh: 对滑板手来说，城市看起来是不一样的。

sentences.en: Something I definitely always do is look for opportunities to skateboard.
sentences.zh: 我绝对会做的一件事就是寻找滑滑板的机会。

sentences.en: But I can't, I can't help myself.
sentences.zh: 但我忍不住，我控制不住自己。

sentences.en: We compulsively look for things like ledges or curb cuts, mundane stuff that people walk right paSt.
sentences.zh: 我们强迫性地寻找像壁架或路缘斜坡这样的东西，那些人们直接走过却视而不见的平凡事物。

sentences.en: But to a skateboarder, even a pole that's been bent by a car is a thing to skate.
sentences.zh: 但对滑板手来说，即使是被车撞弯的柱子也是可以滑的东西。

sentences.en: So you're always on the hunt.
sentences.zh: 所以你总是在搜寻。

sentences.en: Like, I'll make my wife stop the car if I see something new.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我看到什么新鲜的东西，我会让妻子停车。

sentences.en: Dude, I even, like, I even, when I'm watching movies, will be looking for spots.
sentences.zh: 老兄，我甚至，我甚至在看电影的时候，都会寻找滑板点。

sentences.en: You look for spots in movies?
sentences.zh: 你看电影时也会找滑板点？

sentences.en: Whoa, Andrew.
sentences.zh: 哇，安德鲁。

sentences.en: Like, I've watched The Simpsons, and I'm like, you could skate that hubba.
sentences.zh: 比如，我看《辛普森一家》的时候，我会想，那个Hubba（阶梯扶手）是可以滑的。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: I guess I do that, too.
sentences.zh: 我想我也那样做。

sentences.en: Wait, what's a hubba?
sentences.zh: 等等，什么是Hubba？

sentences.en: A hubba is what skaters call a ledge that runs down a flight of stairs parallel to the stairs.
sentences.zh: Hubba是滑板手对那种沿着楼梯平行延伸的壁架的称呼。

sentences.en: And it's named after a famous spot in San Francisco called Hubba Hideout.
sentences.zh: 它以旧金山一个著名的滑板点Hubba Hideout命名。

sentences.en: Hubba is slang for crack.
sentences.zh: Hubba是快克（一种毒品）的俚语。

sentences.en: So I guess people used to hang out there, used to gather there to smoke crack.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜人们过去常在那里闲逛，聚在一起吸食快克。

sentences.en: It's particularly skateboard-worthy?
sentences.zh: 它特别值得滑吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, because it's this perfect ledge that runs parallel down the flight of stairs.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为它是一个完美的壁架，沿着楼梯平行向下延伸。

sentences.en: I mean, ask any skater, go to any skate park.
sentences.zh: 我是说，问任何一个滑板手，去任何一个滑板公园。

sentences.en: You know, every skater will know what a hubba is.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每个滑板手都知道什么是Hubba。

sentences.en: And that is how I'm going to exclusively refer to them from now on.
sentences.zh: 从现在开始，我将只用这个词来称呼它们。

sentences.en: I'm always looking for things like that.
sentences.zh: 我一直在寻找类似的东西。

sentences.en: Black wax kicked on a ledge or wheel marks on a wall.
sentences.zh: 壁架上留下的黑色蜡迹，或者墙上的轮印。

sentences.en: These are little breadcrumb trails left by my people.
sentences.zh: 这些是我的人留下的点点滴滴的线索。

sentences.en: And once you start following these trails, they'll lead you to a turf war between the city and the skaters.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始追踪这些线索，它们就会把你带到城市与滑板手之间的地盘争夺战中。

sentences.en: Oh, this spot here.
sentences.zh: 噢，这个点。

sentences.en: Have you ever skated these?
sentences.zh: 你在这里滑过吗？

sentences.en: This has long been known as a spot to meet up.
sentences.zh: 这里长期以来一直被认为是聚会点。

sentences.en: And more recently, they put some stoppers on it to prevent people from skating.
sentences.zh: 最近，他们安装了一些阻挡器，以防止人们滑板。

sentences.en: So a skate stopper is anything that someone might add to something we'd want to skateboard on to stop us from skateboarding on it.
sentences.zh: 所以滑板阻挡器是指任何被加装在我们想滑的东西上，用来阻止我们滑板的东西。

sentences.en: So in this case, on these long kind of S-shaped granite benches that we're looking at,
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，在我们看到的这些长长的S形花岗岩长椅上，

sentences.en: they put strips of granite kind of running the width of the bench so that we can't ride along the top of it.
sentences.zh: 他们安装了横跨长椅宽度的花岗岩条，这样我们就不能在上面滑行了。

sentences.en: Normally, people would be sliding on this and then hit this or grinding on this and then hit, come to a stop against these.
sentences.zh: 通常，人们会在上面滑行，然后撞到这个，或者在上面研磨（Grind），然后撞到这些东西停下来。

sentences.en: I imagine most people don't know what they're there for.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人不知道它们是干什么用的。

sentences.en: So as skateboarders, I think we're hypersensitive and very aware of these small things that get added.
sentences.zh: 所以作为滑板手，我认为我们对这些被添加的小东西非常敏感，也非常了解。

sentences.en: Well, one of the most traditional type of thing you'll see will be some kind of a metal peg or raised metal attachment
sentences.zh: 嗯，你会看到的最传统的一种东西是某种金属钉或凸起的金属附件，

sentences.en: that is either built into a wall or attached to a wall afterwards.
sentences.zh: 要么是嵌在墙里的，要么是事后安装在墙上的。

sentences.en: And what that does is it creates a discontinuous edge.
sentences.zh: 它的作用是制造一个不连续的边缘。

sentences.en: Tony Bercali is an architect from Philadelphia.
sentences.zh: 托尼·伯卡利是一位来自费城的建筑师。

sentences.en: He's fascinated with how skaters interact with the city.
sentences.zh: 他着迷于滑板手如何与城市互动。

sentences.en: And though he's not a skateboarder himself,
sentences.zh: 虽然他自己不是滑板手，

sentences.en: Tony's always kept tabs on the types of anti-skating measures a city can deploy.
sentences.zh: 但托尼一直关注着城市可以部署的各种反滑板措施。

sentences.en: And then it gets more extreme and more ridiculous where, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后它变得越来越极端，越来越荒谬，你知道，

sentences.en: there are companies that sell things that look like metal seashells and metal crabs
sentences.zh: 有些公司销售看起来像金属贝壳和金属螃蟹的东西，

sentences.en: that I guess for some reason that's meant to be more aesthetically pleasing.
sentences.zh: 我想出于某种原因，那被认为在美学上更令人愉悦。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Those aesthetically pleasing skate stoppers are all around the Embarcadero in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 那些美观的滑板阻挡器遍布旧金山的内河码头。

sentences.en: To Tony, the reason why modern cities are so perfect for skateboarding goes back to a French dude named Le Corbusier.
sentences.zh: 对托尼来说，现代城市之所以如此适合滑板，要追溯到一个叫勒·柯布西耶的法国人。

sentences.en: Tony Bercali wrote an essay called Thanks, Le Corbusier, from the skateboarders.
sentences.zh: 托尼·伯卡利写了一篇名为《谢谢你，勒·柯布西耶，来自滑板手们》的文章。

sentences.en: In it, he contends that Le Corbusier, as the platonic ideal of the modernist architect,
sentences.zh: 在文中，他认为勒·柯布西耶作为现代主义建筑师的柏拉图式理想，

sentences.en: with his cool glasses and love of concrete, is the patron saint of skateboarders.
sentences.zh: 戴着酷酷的眼镜，热爱混凝土，是滑板手的守护神。

sentences.en: Modernists were the ones that reinterpreted a bench in a park as a slab of granite,
sentences.zh: 现代主义者是将公园里的长椅重新诠释为花岗岩板的人，

sentences.en: reinterpreted, you know, kind of flowing landscapes, grassy areas as these kind of paved open plaza spaces.
sentences.zh: 将流动的景观、草地重新诠释为这种铺砌的开放式广场空间的人。

sentences.en: And it just turned out that wide open space with nice granite ledges at the edge made really good skateboarding space.
sentences.zh: 结果证明，带有漂亮花岗岩边缘的宽阔开放空间确实成了很好的滑板空间。

sentences.en: And who would have known?
sentences.zh: 谁能想到呢？

sentences.en: The prime example of modernist landscape architecture that's inadvertently perfect for skateboarding is Philadelphia's Love Park.
sentences.zh: 现代主义景观建筑的典范，无意中完美适合滑板的，是费城的爱之公园。

sentences.en: Its real name is JFK Plaza, but it's called Love Park after Robert Indiana's giant love statue with that slanted O
sentences.zh: 它的真名是肯尼迪广场，但因罗伯特·印第安纳那个带有倾斜字母O的巨大“爱”字雕塑而被称为爱之公园，

sentences.en: that was put there for the United States Bicentennial.
sentences.zh: 那是为美国建国两百周年而放置在那里的。

sentences.en: In the center of Philadelphia is City Hall.
sentences.zh: 费城的中心是市政厅。

sentences.en: And if you draw a line from City Hall to the Art Museum, there's a diagonal boulevard that connects the two.
sentences.zh: 如果你从市政厅画一条线到艺术博物馆，有一条对角线大道连接着两者。

sentences.en: And along that axis is where Love Park was placed.
sentences.zh: 爱之公园就位于这条轴线上。

sentences.en: The two-tiered plaza takes up an entire city block.
sentences.zh: 这个双层广场占据了整个城市街区。

sentences.en: In the center, long, wide steps cascade down to a giant circular fountain.
sentences.zh: 在中心，长而宽的台阶倾泻而下，通向一个巨大的圆形喷泉。

sentences.en: Above, on the main level, granite planters surround the plaza, as well as lots of rectangular marble benches.
sentences.zh: 上方的主层，花岗岩花坛环绕着广场，还有许多长方形的大理石长椅。

sentences.en: It's a space only a modernist or a skateboarder could love.
sentences.zh: 这是一个只有现代主义者或滑板手才会喜欢的空间。

sentences.en: And it's awesome for skating because you can do what we call lines, which is like a series of tricks.
sentences.zh: 它非常适合滑板，因为你可以做我们称之为“线路”的动作，也就是一系列的技巧组合。

sentences.en: So you could do like a switch crook on one of the benches and then a fakie tray flip.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以先在其中一个长椅上做一个Switch Crook（反脚勾研磨），然后做一个Fakie Tray Flip（倒滑翻板）。

sentences.en: And then if you wanted to, you could do like a switchback tail on another part of the park.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意，你可以在公园的另一部分做一个Switchback Tail（反脚尾部研磨）。

sentences.en: Oh, and the granite tiles can even be pried up to make little ramps to launch off of.
sentences.zh: 噢，花岗岩瓷砖甚至可以撬起来做成小坡道来起跳。

sentences.en: The park was conceived for the late Edmund Bacon as part of his undergraduate thesis at Cornell.
sentences.zh: 这个公园是已故的埃德蒙·培根在康奈尔大学读本科时的毕业论文的一部分。

sentences.en: He later made the park a reality as the executive director of the Philadelphia City Planning Commission with the help of architect Vincent Kling.
sentences.zh: 后来，他在建筑师文森特·克林的帮助下，以费城城市规划委员会执行主任的身份将公园变成了现实。

sentences.en: Ed's been a big deal in the architecture world since the 50s, when he shaped how Philly looks today.
sentences.zh: 埃德自50年代以来在建筑界就很有名，当时他塑造了费城今天的样子。

sentences.en: His vision for the city even put him on the cover of Time magazine.
sentences.zh: 他对城市的愿景甚至让他登上了《时代》周刊的封面。

sentences.en: He also happens to be the father of Kevin Bacon.
sentences.zh: 他恰好还是凯文·培根的父亲。

sentences.en: Really.
sentences.zh: 真的。

sentences.en: Now you're one level away from Kevin because you're talking to me, though.
sentences.zh: 现在你离凯文只有一级之遥了，因为你在跟我说话。

sentences.en: And I'm actually, wait, that'd be two, right?
sentences.zh: 其实，等等，那是两级，对吧？

sentences.en: Actually, I think that's four degrees.
sentences.zh: 其实，我认为那是四度（分隔）。

sentences.en: This is the closest I've been in that game.
sentences.zh: 这是我在那个游戏中离他最近的一次。

sentences.en: This is very exciting.
sentences.zh: 这太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: So there you go, my friend.
sentences.zh: 所以就是这样，我的朋友。

sentences.en: I'm happy I could help you there.
sentences.zh: 很高兴我能帮到你。

sentences.en: Bacon's design turned out to be perfect for skateboarding.
sentences.zh: 培根的设计结果证明对滑板来说是完美的。

sentences.en: And in the 80s, when skating took to the streets, the timing was perfect for skaters to claim Love Park as their own.
sentences.zh: 而在80年代，当滑板运动走向街头时，时机恰好让滑板手们将爱之公园据为己有。

sentences.en: You know, there was kind of a suburban migration.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当时有一种郊区化迁移。

sentences.en: There was less interest in density.
sentences.zh: 人们对城市密度的兴趣降低了。

sentences.en: And so places like Love Park were kind of sitting there, not being used.
sentences.zh: 所以像爱之公园这样的地方就那样闲置着，没有被使用。

sentences.en: In the early 90s, skaters started filming themselves at Love Park.
sentences.zh: 90年代初，滑板手们开始在爱之公园拍摄自己的视频。

sentences.en: And the videos found their way to the epicenter of the skate world, California.
sentences.zh: 这些视频传到了滑板世界的中心——加利福尼亚。

sentences.en: Suddenly, Philadelphia was a destination for skaters.
sentences.zh: 突然间，费城成了滑板手的目的地。

sentences.en: And as the skateboarding industry grew, so did the popularity of Love Park.
sentences.zh: 随着滑板产业的发展，爱之公园的知名度也随之提高。

sentences.en: By the late 90s, pro skaters moved to Philly just to skate it every day.
sentences.zh: 到了90年代末，职业滑板手搬到费城，只为了每天在那里滑板。

sentences.en: They built their careers shooting photos for glossy skateboard magazines at the park.
sentences.zh: 他们通过为光鲜亮丽的滑板杂志拍摄公园照片来建立自己的职业生涯。

sentences.en: You could even virtually skate there in Tony Hawk's famous video game.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以在托尼·霍克著名的电子游戏中虚拟地在那里滑板。

sentences.en: So as an awkward 14-year-old passing through Philly on vacation, I was like,
sentences.zh: 所以作为一个尴尬的14岁少年，在度假经过费城时，我说：

sentences.en: Dad, we gotta go to Love Park.
sentences.zh: 爸爸，我们得去爱之公园。

sentences.en: So I got to skate the ledges and stairs I saw on videos and on my PlayStation while my dad read the newspaper by the fountain.
sentences.zh: 于是我得以在视频和PlayStation上看到的壁架和楼梯上滑板，而我爸爸在喷泉边看报纸。

sentences.en: I wouldn't be that excited again until I got my braces off.
sentences.zh: 直到我摘掉牙套，我再也没有那么兴奋过。

sentences.en: Even though Love Park was like Mecca, it was never legal to skate there.
sentences.zh: 尽管爱之公园就像麦加圣地，但在那里滑板从来都不是合法的。

sentences.en: I don't think it's legal to skate at Mecca either.
sentences.zh: 我不认为在麦加滑板也是合法的。

sentences.en: Skaters would get tackled by cops, ticketed by undercovers, or have their boards taken away.
sentences.zh: 滑板手会被警察扑倒，被便衣开罚单，或者滑板被没收。

sentences.en: And the area was gentrifying.
sentences.zh: 而且该地区正在中产阶级化。

sentences.en: Finally, in 2002, Philly Mayor John Street took the skateboard band a step further and renovated the park.
sentences.zh: 最终，在2002年，费城市长约翰·斯特里特将滑板禁令更进一步，翻修了公园。

sentences.en: The major thing that they did was they removed all of the granite benches, these great skatable elements.
sentences.zh: 他们所做的主要事情是拆除了所有的花岗岩长椅，这些伟大的可滑元素。

sentences.en: And they replaced them with, you know, kind of Williams and Sonoma-ish looking wood benches
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是，你知道，那种看起来像威廉姆斯-索诺玛风格的木制长椅，

sentences.en: that look like they belong in an 1890s kind of park.
sentences.zh: 看起来像是属于1890年代的公园。

sentences.en: Disguised as decoration, the new features were meant to make it harder for skaters to use the ledges
sentences.zh: 伪装成装饰品，这些新设施旨在让滑板手更难利用壁架，

sentences.en: or to cruise from one end of the park to the other.
sentences.zh: 或者从公园的一端滑行到另一端。

sentences.en: So they took away the wide open paved areas and tried to replace them with grassy spaces in between.
sentences.zh: 所以他们拆除了宽阔的铺砌区域，试图用中间的草地空间来代替它们。

sentences.en: You know, adding some landscaping, adding an actual lawn was a good idea,
sentences.zh: 你知道，增加一些景观，增加一片真正的草坪是个好主意，

sentences.en: but the design result was kind of horrible.
sentences.zh: 但设计结果却有点糟糕。

sentences.en: It's just a very uncomfortable space and not a space that people want to use.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常不舒服的空间，不是人们想要使用的空间。

sentences.en: People protested the renovations.
sentences.zh: 人们抗议了这次翻修。

sentences.en: There were rallies and newspaper articles.
sentences.zh: 有集会和报纸文章。

sentences.en: One story read,
sentences.zh: 一篇报道写道：

sentences.en: The mayor blindly took a route of time-honored Philadelphia tradition
sentences.zh: 市长盲目地采取了一种费城悠久的传统路线，

sentences.en: in destroying a source of pride and fame, hard-earned by its own citizens.
sentences.zh: 摧毁了其公民辛苦赢得的自豪感和名声的源泉。

sentences.en: A big skateboard shoe company called DC even offered up a million dollars to keep the park the way it was
sentences.zh: 一家名为DC的大型滑板鞋公司甚至出资一百万美元来保持公园原样，

sentences.en: and to kind of offset any damages skaters might have done over the years.
sentences.zh: 并抵消滑板手多年来可能造成的任何损害。

sentences.en: The city of Philadelphia declined the offer.
sentences.zh: 费城市政府拒绝了这一提议。

sentences.en: City councillors and architects like Tony spoke out too.
sentences.zh: 市议员和像托尼这样的建筑师也发出了反对的声音。

sentences.en: I think there would have been a way to make some significant adjustments to Love Park
sentences.zh: 我认为本来是有办法对爱公园进行一些重大调整的，

sentences.en: that would accommodate other kinds of activities without totally compromising skateboarding
sentences.zh: 既能容纳其他类型的活动，又不会完全损害滑板运动，

sentences.en: and come up with a successful evolution of the space.
sentences.zh: 并能让这个空间实现成功的演变。

sentences.en: I think that that would have been possible.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是完全可能的。

sentences.en: I think politically that would have been too difficult.
sentences.zh: 但在政治上，我认为那太难了。

sentences.en: Love Park drew people to the city.
sentences.zh: 爱公园曾吸引人们来到这座城市。

sentences.en: Philadelphia even hosted this big skateboard competition called the X Games,
sentences.zh: 费城甚至还举办过一场名为“X运动会”的大型滑板比赛，

sentences.en: the two summers prior to getting rid of Love Park.
sentences.zh: 就在拆除爱公园前的两个夏天。

sentences.en: But, you know, unlike traditional sports,
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，与传统体育项目不同，

sentences.en: skateboarding is kind of hard to control and difficult to monetize.
sentences.zh: 滑板运动很难控制，也很难商业化。

sentences.en: And that's usually a little scary to the squares.
sentences.zh: 而这通常会让那些循规蹈矩的人感到害怕。

sentences.en: But not to Ed Bacon.
sentences.zh: 但埃德·培根（Ed Bacon）却不这么认为。

sentences.en: Bacon was thrilled that his space was evolving.
sentences.zh: 培根对自己的空间能够演变感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Here he is from a 2006 documentary called Freedom of Space.
sentences.zh: 这是他在2006年一部名为《空间的自由》的纪录片中的片段。

sentences.en: I think skateboarding is a far more profound revolution than people give it credit.
sentences.zh: 我认为滑板运动是一场比人们所认为的要深刻得多的革命。

sentences.en: The wonderful thing to me is that these young people discovered that they themselves
sentences.zh: 对我来说，最美妙的事情是这些年轻人发现他们自己

sentences.en: would creatively adapt to the environment they already found.
sentences.zh: 能够创造性地适应他们所处的环境。

sentences.en: And that it was their joy to adapt themselves physically to what was already there.
sentences.zh: 而且他们乐于在身体上适应现有的环境。

sentences.en: Bacon was so against the renovations and cracked down on skaters in his park,
sentences.zh: 培根非常反对翻新工程，并严厉打击公园里的滑手，

sentences.en: he staged his own proteSt.
sentences.zh: 他甚至策划了自己的抗议活动。

sentences.en: On October 8, 2002, with the media there,
sentences.zh: 2002年10月8日，在媒体的见证下，

sentences.en: two people propping him up on either side,
sentences.zh: 两边各有人搀扶着他，

sentences.en: and a blue bicycle helmet on.
sentences.zh: 头上戴着一顶蓝色自行车头盔。

sentences.en: A white-haired, trench coat-clad, 92-year-old Ed Bacon
sentences.zh: 92岁高龄、满头白发、身穿风衣的埃德·培根

sentences.en: rode a skateboard in Love Park.
sentences.zh: 在爱公园里滑起了滑板。

sentences.en: Held up and pushed along on a skateboard might be a more accurate description.
sentences.zh: 准确地说，应该是被人搀扶着在滑板上滑行。

sentences.en: And now I, Edmund Dunn Bacon, in total defiance of Mayor Good,
sentences.zh: “现在我，埃德蒙·邓恩·培根，完全无视市长古德（Mayor Good），

sentences.en: I've gone in total defiance of Mayor Street and the Council of the City of Philadelphia,
sentences.zh: 我完全无视斯特里特市长（Mayor Street）和费城市议会，

sentences.en: hereby exercise my rights as a citizen of the United States,
sentences.zh: 在此行使我作为美国公民的权利，

sentences.en: and I deliberately skate in my beloved Love Park.
sentences.zh: 我特意在我心爱的爱公园里滑滑板。”

sentences.en: Oh, God!
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪！

sentences.en: Thank you, thank you, thank you!
sentences.zh: 谢谢，谢谢，谢谢！

sentences.en: My whole damn life has been worth it just for this moment.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子能有这一刻，一切都值了。

sentences.en: The ugly pink planters and William & Sonoma benches still Gray Slope Park,
sentences.zh: 那些丑陋的粉色花坛和威廉索诺玛（William & Sonoma）长椅依然占据着爱公园，

sentences.en: but so does a plaque memorializing Ed Bacon.
sentences.zh: 但纪念埃德·培根的牌匾也依然在那里。

sentences.en: And people still skateboard there, and they still get chased by cops.
sentences.zh: 人们依然在那里滑滑板，也依然会被警察追赶。

sentences.en: Skaters now figure out ways to work around the redesign,
sentences.zh: 现在的滑手们想出了绕过这些重新设计的方法，

sentences.en: something Ed Bacon would probably be proud of.
sentences.zh: 这大概是埃德·培根会感到自豪的事情。

sentences.en: Love Park isn't the iconic spot it used to be,
sentences.zh: 爱公园不再是曾经那个标志性的地点了，

sentences.en: but skate park started copying features from its original design.
sentences.zh: 但滑板公园开始模仿它最初设计中的元素。

sentences.en: There's a good chance that if a skate park was built in your area in the last 10 years,
sentences.zh: 很有可能，如果过去10年里你所在的地区建了滑板公园，

sentences.en: it'll have a knee-high modernist-style bench,
sentences.zh: 它一定会有那种膝盖高度的现代主义风格长椅，

sentences.en: or maybe even those same cascading long steps like the ones at Love Park.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至有像爱公园那样层叠的长台阶。

sentences.en: You'll also see things like hubba's, like we talked about earlier,
sentences.zh: 你还会看到像我们之前提到的那种“Hubba”障碍物，

sentences.en: or even a low block of concrete beside a small set of stairs.
sentences.zh: 或者小楼梯旁边的低矮混凝土块。

sentences.en: We call that a Pier 7 ledge, named after another San Francisco spot.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为“7号码头（Pier 7）”边缘，是以旧金山的另一个地点命名的。

sentences.en: These are all design elements that were dreamt up by some well-meaning city planner,
sentences.zh: 这些都是由一些好心的城市规划师构思出来的设计元素，

sentences.en: and they're now worshipped by skaters.
sentences.zh: 而现在它们被滑手们奉为圣地。

sentences.en: Tony, the architect we heard from,
sentences.zh: 我们刚才采访的建筑师托尼（Tony），

sentences.en: is now working on a skate-friendly city plaza that's right near Love Park.
sentences.zh: 目前正在设计一个就在爱公园附近的滑板友好型城市广场。

sentences.en: I gotta admit, part of me thinks these designated places to skateboard kind of miss the point.
sentences.zh: 我得承认，我内心深处觉得这些指定的滑板场所似乎偏离了重点。

sentences.en: It's like running a marathon on a treadmill.
sentences.zh: 这就像是在跑步机上跑马拉松。

sentences.en: It's not exactly the type of thing that'll get you on the cover of Runner's World.
sentences.zh: 这可不是那种能让你登上《跑者世界》封面的事情。

sentences.en: But guys like Tony are legitimizing skating to designers and to architects.
sentences.zh: 但像托尼这样的人正在让滑板运动在设计师和建筑师眼中变得合法化。

sentences.en: He gets it.
sentences.zh: 他懂这个。

sentences.en: A skate park is now something that real architects can have a hand in.
sentences.zh: 滑板公园现在成了真正的建筑师可以参与设计的项目。

sentences.en: But part of the excitement of street skating is happening upon that spot
sentences.zh: 但街头滑板的部分乐趣在于偶然发现那个地点，

sentences.en: that wasn't meant to be skated, but seems like it was built exactly for a certain trick.
sentences.zh: 它本不是为了滑板而建的，却看起来像是专门为某种动作而设计的。

sentences.en: It's like found art.
sentences.zh: 这就像是现成的艺术品。

sentences.en: That's why we're still hunting for spots in the streets.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们还在街头寻找场地。

sentences.en: Pro skaters now fly out to China for three weeks at a time
sentences.zh: 职业滑手们现在一次飞往中国三周，

sentences.en: to skate the new sprawling marble plazas that seem to pop up there on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 去滑那些每天似乎都在涌现的新型大理石广场。

sentences.en: And because skateboarding isn't as popular there,
sentences.zh: 而且因为滑板运动在那里还没那么普及，

sentences.en: the war on skaters hasn't seemed to reach China yet.
sentences.zh: 针对滑手的战争似乎还没有波及到中国。

sentences.en: Modernist architecture appears, then skaters, then skate stoppers.
sentences.zh: 现代主义建筑出现，然后是滑手，接着是防滑装置。

sentences.en: And in a way, without really knowing it, we're kind of critiquing the design.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我们在不知不觉中对这种设计进行了批判。

sentences.en: Skaters say, we don't care what you made it for, this is how we're using it.
sentences.zh: 滑手们说，我们不在乎你建造它的初衷是什么，我们就是这样使用它的。

sentences.en: And when you land a trick there, it's like a secret victory.
sentences.zh: 当你在那里完成一个动作时，那就像是一场秘密的胜利。

sentences.en: You put your own mark on a place.
sentences.zh: 你在一个地方留下了自己的印记。

sentences.en: And now even us squares can read those marks too.
sentences.zh: 现在，连我们这些循规蹈矩的人也能读懂这些印记了。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Andrew Norton.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99%隐形》（99% Invisible）由安德鲁·诺顿（Andrew Norton）制作。

sentences.en: I don't know if a lot of radio shows really like to mention smoking crack at the front of their show.
sentences.zh: 我不知道有多少广播节目喜欢在开头提到吸食快克毒品。

sentences.en: With help from Sam Greenspan and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 感谢萨姆·格林斯潘（Sam Greenspan）和我的协助，我是罗曼·马尔斯（Roman Mars）。

sentences.en: It's a project of 91.7 Local Public Radio KALW in San Francisco
sentences.zh: 这是旧金山91.7本地公共广播电台KALW的一个项目，

sentences.en: and the American Institute of Architects in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 也是美国建筑师协会旧金山分会的一个项目。

sentences.en: You can find the show and like the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到并关注这个节目。

sentences.en: I tweet at Roman Mars, but we'll have pictures of Hubba hideouts,
sentences.zh: 我的推特账号是Roman Mars，但我们会在网上发布Hubba隐藏地点的照片，

sentences.en: skaters bounding over Love Park as photographed by Mike Blayback,
sentences.zh: 迈克·布莱巴克（Mike Blayback）拍摄的滑手在爱公园跳跃的照片，

sentences.en: and the amazing video of Edmund Bacon, Define Authority on a Skateboard,
sentences.zh: 以及埃德蒙·培根那段精彩的视频《滑板上的权威定义》，

sentences.en: courtesy of our friends at WHYY.
sentences.zh: 感谢我们在WHYY的朋友提供素材。

sentences.en: Oh God!
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪！

sentences.en: Thank you!
sentences.zh: 谢谢！

sentences.en: Thank you!
sentences.zh: 谢谢！

sentences.en: Thank you!
sentences.zh: 谢谢！

sentences.en: It's all at 99percentinvisible.org.
sentences.zh: 所有内容都在99percentinvisible.org上。

sentences.en: This, I feel like this, what Ed Bacon says here,
sentences.zh: 我觉得这段话，埃德·培根在这里说的这段话，

sentences.en: should be like the Pledge of Allegiance for Skateboarders.
sentences.zh: 应该成为滑手们的“效忠誓词”。

sentences.en: Like, whenever you go skateboard, you should be like,
sentences.zh: 比如，每当你去滑滑板时，你应该说：

sentences.en: I, Andrew Norton, hereby exercise my right as a citizen of Canada,
sentences.zh: “我，安德鲁·诺顿，在此行使我作为加拿大公民的权利，

sentences.en: and I deliberately skateboard.
sentences.zh: 我特意去滑滑板。”

sentences.en: Radiotopia.
sentences.zh: Radiotopia。
